v1_human_g2_ac.ac_1: Given a calendar with events at some times, when searching for a 30 min window then the system returns a list that is in between there time of
v1_human_g2_ac.ac_2: Given an empty calendar when searching for a 60 minute window on a certain day then system will return all available time slot
v1_human_g2_ac.ac_3: Given a calendar with continuous events when searching for a 30 min window then the system will return an empty list
v1_human_g2_ac.ac_4: Given a calendar with events that leave a 60 minute window, when searching for a 120 min window then the system will return a empty list
v1_human_g2_ac.ac_5: Given a calendar with back to back events but available time v2_human, when searching for a 30 min window then the system will return the slots v2_human the events
v1_human_g2_ac.ac_6: Given a 60 min gap between events but a 120 gap onward, then the system is looking for a 120 min window, then the system will return the 120 min slot

v1_human_g2_constraints.c_1: The system operates within the business hours defined, so the available time slots must fall within the business hours
v1_human_g2_constraints.c_2: All the times must follow HH:MM - HH:MM 24 hour
v1_human_g2_constraints.c_3: Calendar events in the input slot do not overlap each other
v1_human_g2_constraints.c_4: Meeting duration is specified in minutes
v1_human_g2_constraints.c_6: Available time slot can start right v2_human an event ends

v1_human_g2_goal: The system needs to output available time slots based on existing events, find a meeting time and date that works given duration and existing events
v1_human_g2_input: list of events; Array of dict[str,str] Dictionary[str,str] meeting duration; integer, int day; Str
v1_human_g2_output: list of short times; Array[list of Strs]
